issues.observed: The four KPI cards show only £2.44M, 42.1%, 109.6%, and 14. Their business labels are absent, so executives cannot reliably distinguish Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth, and Risk Areas.
issues.desired: Each card should have a persistent, clearly readable KPI title, correctly formatted value, and optional concise comparison context.
issues.action: Enable category labels or add card titles for Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth, and Risk Areas. Use currency, percentage, and integer formats appropriate to each measure; do not infer meaning through card position alone.

issues.observed: MonthName is ordered alphabetically or by an unrelated field rather than chronologically, producing the sequence April, August, December, February, and so on. Connecting these categories with a line creates a false time trajectory.
issues.desired: Months should run in fiscal or calendar sequence, with the selected date context made explicit.
issues.action: Sort MonthName by a numeric MonthNumber or FiscalMonthIndex column. Prefer a continuous month-start date axis when multiple years are displayed, and verify the fiscal-year sequence.

issues.observed: The Gross Margin trend uses the same nonchronological MonthName ordering, making direction and year-over-year movement analytically misleading.
issues.desired: A chronological monthly trend that supports valid comparison across the selected fiscal years.
issues.action: Apply the same model-level month sort used for Revenue Trend and use a date-based axis where possible.

issues.observed: TotalRevenue and YoYGrowthPct appear to share one scale in the regional chart. Revenue bars dominate while the percentage series is effectively compressed into a nearly invisible red mark.
issues.desired: Revenue and growth should both be interpretable despite having different units and magnitudes.
issues.action: Use a native line-and-clustered-column chart with TotalRevenue on the primary currency axis and YoYGrowthPct on a secondary percentage axis. Add concise labels and conditional red/green formatting for growth.

issues.observed: The category visual combines revenue and growth on an apparently shared horizontal scale, leaving the YoYGrowthPct encoding nearly invisible and preventing meaningful comparison.
issues.desired: A ranked category view in which revenue magnitude and growth rate are independently legible.
issues.action: Use a supported dual-scale combination or split the metrics into two tightly aligned visuals. Keep horizontal revenue bars for category readability and show growth as labeled percentages with positive and negative conditional colours.

issues.observed: A prominent Power BI trial-capacity banner appears across the top of the deployed report.
issues.desired: A production presentation without licensing or trial notices competing with the executive content.
issues.action: Publish through appropriately licensed production capacity or remove the unsupported trial embedding configuration before board-level distribution.

issues.observed: A large empty green header occupies valuable space without a page title, reporting period, refresh timestamp, or executive message.
issues.desired: A compact header identifying the page and current reporting context.
issues.action: Reduce the header height and add Executive Overview, the active reporting period, and a subtle last-refresh timestamp. Reallocate recovered space to improve chart height and labels.

issues.observed: Thick saturated-green borders and bands surround nearly every object. They dominate the measures, create visual noise, and make the page resemble a development layout rather than a board report.
issues.desired: A restrained neutral canvas with colour reserved for data meaning, exceptions, and selected states.
issues.action: Replace heavy green frames with white or light-neutral surfaces, subtle 1 px borders, and consistent spacing. Retain green only for positive performance and red for adverse performance or risk.

issues.observed: The value 14 has no visible Risk Areas label, severity cue, threshold, or comparison, so its urgency and direction are unknown.
issues.desired: A clearly identified risk count with explicit adverse-state styling and decision context.
issues.action: Label the card Risk Areas, format the count as an integer, and use red only when the measure breaches an approved threshold. Add a comparison such as change versus prior period if a semantically valid measure exists.

issues.observed: The KPI row contains no prior-period variance, target status, trend indicator, or explanatory subtitle.
issues.desired: At-a-glance context showing whether each headline metric is improving, deteriorating, or off target.
issues.action: Add semantically valid YoY or target variances beneath the headline values. Use directional icons and conditional colours only after defining whether an increase is favourable for each KPI.

issues.observed: The slicers are aligned in one row, but use technical field labels such as FiscalPeriod, RegionName, and CategoryName. There is no visible reset control, and the current view is narrowly filtered to FY 2022, London, and Beauty.
issues.desired: Business-friendly filters with an obvious way to return to the approved executive default view.
issues.action: Rename slicer titles to Fiscal Period, Region, and Category; add a Reset filters bookmark button; and define a deliberate default executive state. Preserve the visible selection context rather than silently removing valid filters.

issues.observed: Regional Performance shows only London and Scotland, while Category Performance shows only Beauty and Childrenswear. This may be a valid filter result, but it limits the comprehensive retail overview expected for CEO/CFO use.
issues.desired: The default page should provide an enterprise-wide comparison while still allowing drill-down selections.
issues.action: Verify that the deployed default slicer state is intentionally scoped. If not, clear restrictive defaults and open on all regions and categories. Do not override user selections or alter measure semantics.

issues.observed: Visual titles expose model-oriented names such as TotalRevenue, GrossMarginPct, MonthName, and FiscalYear rather than executive language.
issues.desired: Concise business titles such as Revenue Trend, Gross Margin % Trend, Regional Performance, and Category Performance.
issues.action: Set custom visual titles and legend labels using business-friendly terminology. Keep technical field names out of the presentation layer.

issues.observed: Axis labels, legends, and chart titles are small and low-contrast, particularly in the compressed bottom row. Several month labels are truncated.
issues.desired: Boardroom-readable labels that remain clear on a shared screen or exported page.
issues.action: Increase title, legend, and axis font sizes; use higher-contrast text; reduce unnecessary legend wording; and provide enough visual height to avoid label truncation.

issues.observed: The broad single revenue chart and three compressed lower charts create an unbalanced grid. The Gross Margin trend receives much less space than Revenue Trend despite being an expected peer visual.
issues.desired: A balanced analytical grid with the two trends side by side and the two comparison visuals side by side.
issues.action: Adopt a consistent two-column chart grid beneath the KPI row. Give Revenue Trend and Gross Margin % Trend equal dimensions, then place Regional and Category Performance in an equally aligned row.

issues.observed: Revenue is shown as £2.44M with no indication of reporting currency or whether the unit is appropriate for enterprise scale.
issues.desired: A consistently formatted executive value with explicit currency context.
issues.action: Confirm the measure's reporting currency and use a consistent display unit across the card and charts. Add a page-level currency note where the business operates across currencies.

issues.observed: The page presents series and bars but does not clearly surface the worst region, declining category, threshold breach, or major change requiring executive action.
issues.desired: A visual narrative that directs attention to material growth drivers and risks.
issues.action: Sort comparison charts by a meaningful metric, apply restrained exception-based conditional formatting, and add a short dynamic insight subtitle only when backed by validated measures.

issues.observed: Cards use visible corner artifacts and heavy framing, with limited internal spacing and no consistent surface treatment.
issues.desired: Clean, evenly padded KPI surfaces with subtle boundaries and consistent alignment.
issues.action: Remove decorative corner shapes, standardize card padding, and use subtle borders or shadows supported by the Power BI theme.

summary: The actual page contains the required KPI, trend, regional, and category concepts, and most structural improvements are feasible with native Power BI. However, missing KPI labels, nonchronological month axes, ineffective mixed-unit charts, technical naming, heavy green framing, and a visible trial banner substantially undermine analytical validity and executive credibility. The highest priorities are to correct time ordering, separate revenue and percentage scales, identify every KPI, and rebuild the page hierarchy with a restrained production theme.
reference_rejected_ideas: Pixel-perfect replication of the Power BI service chrome, left navigation rail, and top application toolbar is not necessary for analytical quality and may be controlled by the host or embedding environment.

Embedding a sparkline inside every KPI card exactly as shown may require the newer card visual, layering, or custom visuals; a validated variance and status indicator is an acceptable native alternative.

The reference's category revenue bars with independently positioned growth dots are not a straightforward native clustered bar configuration. A supported combo treatment or two aligned visuals is preferable to forcing unlike units onto one axis.
Decorative information icons on every card are unnecessary unless they open useful metric definitions or tooltip content.
Reference-specific monetary scale, date range, regions, and categories should not be copied because the deployed report must retain its actual data, filters, currency, and measure semantics.
